key_insight: PhenOM, a single foundation model for medical-event prediction—not cancer drug discovery—validated thousands of predictive tasks spanning more than 1,770 outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The model could support patient-level risk assessment and screening across clinical domains, but the abstract does not establish benefits for clinical decisions or patient outcomes.
method: Trained on longitudinal medical-event data from more than 400 million patient records.
Evaluated Future Risk, Screening, Care Opportunity, and Treatment Effect tasks.
Defined eligible populations and outcomes using standardized medical codes where possible.
evidence_signal: On data excluded from training, 80% of predictive tasks achieved AUROC ≥0.70 and 30% achieved ≥0.80; the paper presents 177 example tasks.
watch_item: Performance varied by outcome and domain; held-out AUROC alone does not establish calibration, external generalizability, or clinical utility.
paper_title: Performance of a foundation model to generate thousands of predicted outcomes across multiple use cases
